subject: MAP cadence incident: procurement hold and rebaseline proposal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cardinalhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP cadence concern — procurement hold impact (Q1 MAP attached)

Hi Sarah / team,

Quick heads up — during this morning's call you mentioned the procurement hold while the finance committee finishes the FY26 budget review. We discussed a provisional two-week pause on purchase order issuance. That pause materially shifts the MAP milestones tied to the procurement milestone on Apr 7; with a two-week delay we move into an acceptance window that overlaps with a compliance audit on your side.

Attached: Q1-MAP-v3.xlsx (current MAP export from our tracker) — highlights in column D the procurement milestone and downstream cutover dates.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm the expected duration of the hold (two weeks vs open-ended)?
- If two weeks, can we get tentative PO issuance by 21 Mar to preserve the planned Pilot window?
- If open-ended, we need to propose a re-baselined MAP and a short mitigation plan (temporary scope hold + extended acceptance window).

We can jump on a 30-minute triage today; Marissa and Rishi are available late afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Cardinal Health Procurement <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Mar 2025 13:38:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP cadence concern — procurement hold impact (Q1 MAP attached)

Diego — thanks for pulling this together and for the attachment. Apologies, this came up late — our finance committee has a tranche review the week of 10 Mar and procurement has been asked to pause non-critical PO processing until that completes. At this point we're expecting a two-week window but I can't give hard certainty until the 12th.

Immediate notes from our side:
- Procurement will not finalize the PO until the committee signs off; that likely pushes PO to ~21 Mar earliest.
- We still intend to run the pilot in late April but we need the SOW and a revised timeline to present alongside the PO request.
- Can you produce a redlined SOW and a short rebaseline that shows a conservative plan (30-day shift) and a fallback (45-day) so we can present options?

I'll be on the triage call this afternoon if that still works.

Best,
Sarah Levin
Director, Digital Programs | Cardinal Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Mar 2025 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP cadence concern — procurement hold impact (Q1 MAP attached)

Diego / team — catching up after the call. Short internal summary and recommended next steps: 

Impact assessment (high level):
- Procurement hold -> PO slip to 21 Mar: Pilot kickoff slides ~2–3 weeks; acceptance window compresses into May maintenance blackout on Cardinal side. Risk: missing compliance remediation window and delaying GA.
- If hold goes longer than two weeks, we should expect a minimum 30-day push on go-live.

Recommended actions:
1) Produce two rebaseline options (Conservative = 30-day shift; Contingency = 45-day shift) with revised MAP and clear owners per milestone.
2) Prepare an SOW addendum that isolates scope items that unblock pilot vs GA (so Cardinal can sign the pilot scope sooner).
3) Propose a credit cadence / timing contingency to protect Cardinal if the hold becomes a month+ delay (we can discuss % of monthly committed capacity credits).
4) Escalate to Rishi / sales leadership if we need credit approval or contract flexibility; Hannah can weigh in on SLA/credit exceptions.

I can have draft rebaseline and the SOW addendum by EOD tomorrow if Diego and Rishi are ok with the proposed credit framing.

-Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Mar 2025 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: MAP rebaseline request + proposed mitigation (need leadership signoff)

Team — tagging for decision. Per Cardinal's note this morning, procurement will likely move PO to 21 Mar; they asked for two rebaseline options. Marissa has volunteered to produce the drafts by EOD tomorrow. I'm proposing we standardize the escalation packet to include:

1) Executive summary (1 page) describing the trigger (procurement hold), impact window, and recommended rebaseline (Conservative = +30d; Contingency = +45d).
2) MAP export with new dates (attached as rebaseline-proposal.pdf).
3) SOW addendum that splits Pilot scope vs GA scope (drafted by Camila).
4) Credit proposal table: two options (pro-rated monthly credit; or consumption buffer for agreed pilot window).
5) Customer slide with ask: "Recommend PO by 21 Mar or sign pilot addendum by 12 Mar to hold original Pilot window."

Decision points I need from leadership:
- Approve the credit framework (I recommend starting with a 10% pro-rated buffer for up to 30 days; escalate if >30d).
- Approve that we offer the SOW addendum path to allow Cardinal to sign for pilot-only work.

If you approve, I'll send the packet to Sarah and schedule the follow-up with procurement (I recommend Thu 6 Mar or Fri 7 Mar).

Attachments: rebaseline-proposal.pdf
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ CARD-4921
DocuSign (proposal draft): https://docusign.com/sign/CARD-4921-proposal

Thanks — Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
